acceptanceCriteria: The leak is reproduced or the cause is confirmed, and every test-created keeper socketpair is close-on-exec under ForkLock like production.
A keeper whose test process exits is gone within a bounded time; a maintained test, or a cleanup in the test that spawns the keeper, proves it.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator session.

Observed 2026-10-06 on the owner's macOS host: process `cem01-go.test __cem01-stable-keeper/1` (pid 5049, parent launchd, alone in its own process group, state SN, 0% CPU) had been running for 4 days 23 hours from an already-deleted go-build directory under /var/folders/.../T. It exited on SIGTERM when the owner asked for cleanup. stableKeeperMain (interop/cem01-go/stable_process_darwin.go) blocks reading fd 3 until the owner end of its socketpair reaches EOF, then kills its group; so the owner end stayed open somewhere for days.

Suspected cause (inferred from source, not reproduced): the darwin keeper test (stable_process_darwin_test.go, around line 270) creates its socketpair with plain syscall.Socketpair, without syscall.ForkLock and CloseOnExec, unlike production at stable_process_darwin.go:268-274. A child process started concurrently by another test can inherit the owner fd and keep the keeper alive after the test exits. Which test run produced pid 5049 was not observed.
